lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the card shop table, Daisy has already laid out a deck and is waiting for you to take the seat across from her.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: That's my table. You're welcome to share it, unless you're going to shuffle like a lawn mower.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I was about to say the same about your deck sleeves.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Oh, so you do have a personality. Good. I was worried I'd have to supply both sides of the conversation.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You always test new people like this?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Only the ones who look like they might actually surprise me. One game. No spectators. Deal?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: And if I win?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Then you get to choose our rematch location. If I win, you stop pretending you're not curious.

choices.label: Accept the match without bargaining
choices.reply: No hesitation. I like that. Now don't complain when I make you work for it.

choices.label: Ask what she gets out of testing strangers
choices.reply: Someone who can lose gracefully and win without being cruel. Your answer just earned you a point.

choices.label: Say you'd have come over even without the challenge
choices.reply: Bold answer. I was hoping you'd say it, but don't let that distract you from your opening hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the café window, Daisy holds two fabric sketches up to the daylight so you can compare their layers and color.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: I brought two sketches, and before you ask, they aren't new deck boxes.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You asked me here to judge outfits?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: I asked you here because you'll tell me if something doesn't work. Most people just say 'pretty' and stop looking.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: The burgundy fabric is almost transparent.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: That's why it has a lining. There's a difference between showing your style and leaving everything to chance.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Here—hold this edge up to the window. See how the color changes?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I see why you wanted a second pair of eyes.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: And maybe I wanted an excuse to see you without a card table between us. Don't get a big head.

choices.label: Point out the way the lining makes the color warmer
choices.reply: You actually looked. That's worth more than a hundred automatic compliments.

choices.label: Admit you're not an expert but offer to help test the fabric
choices.reply: Perfect. Honest and useful. A dangerous combination.

choices.label: Tell her the clothes are great, but she steals the scene
choices.reply: Careful. Keep saying things like that and I'll start thinking you mean them.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Don't laugh. This hoodie could fit two of me. That's the point.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I almost didn't recognize you.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Exactly. Everyone expects me to deliver a punch line or a perfect entrance. Today I wanted to lose a game anonymously and get terrible vending-machine coffee.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Something happened?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: A stranger photographed me without asking and posted it around town. Everyone had a theory about who I was. Nobody thought to ask.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: That sounds exhausting.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: I can dress boldly and still want boundaries. Both can be true.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Do you want me to do something?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Just stay here a minute. And maybe beat me at this game so I can complain about something normal.

choices.label: Let her decide whether to report the photo
choices.reply: Thank you. I needed a choice that was mine for a change.

choices.label: Ask what would make her feel comfortable tonight
choices.reply: This. Not having to perform. Maybe one more round.

choices.label: Challenge her to the arcade machine, no questions asked
choices.reply: There you are. My favorite kind of distraction: one that actually understands the assignment.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: I found a quiet corner in the café where nobody asks for a photo or a performance.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: And you brought me there.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: You have learned the difference between looking at me and actually paying attention.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: That sounds like a difficult lesson.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: It was. I used to think being noticed was the same as being known.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You do not have to be on with me.

choices.label: Ask what she wants people to know about her
choices.response: That I choose my own image. The rest is earned, not assumed.

choices.label: Tell her you respect the person behind the presentation
choices.response: Good. Then keep talking to me like I am a person, not a story you invented.

choices.label: Say you like the version of her that surprises you
choices.response: Careful. That sounds like you are getting to know me on purpose.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: In the quiet park at dusk, Daisy sits beside you and turns the conversation toward the lotus tattoo she chose for herself.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Do you remember asking me about the flower tattoo?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: The one in the middle of your chest?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Yeah. I got it after a year when I thought nothing would feel steady again. It's a lotus—messy roots, beautiful bloom. Very dramatic. Very me.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: And the stars?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: People who stayed when I was hard to be around. I don't give everyone that story.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Why tell me now?

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: Because you stopped trying to guess who I am from what I wear. You kept showing up for the actual person.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I'm glad you told me.

lines.speaker: daisy
lines.text: So am I. I'm usually the first person to turn something serious into a joke. You can have one sincere answer today. Ask me something that matters.

choices.label: Tell her she never owes you an explanation
choices.reply: Good. Then I can tell you things because I want to, not because I have to.

choices.label: Share a time you had to start over too
choices.reply: That sounded difficult to say. Thank you for trusting me with it.

choices.label: Ask whether you can hold her hand
choices.reply: Yes. Just... don't turn it into a victory pose, okay?
